anomaly_def.Name: Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly : Sessions serialize on hot buffer-cache pages and the latches protecting them, producing buffer-busy/page-latch waits and spin loops inside the buffer manager.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database processes consume nearly all available CPU cycles, pushing system-wide utilization and run-queue lengths to saturation levels.

When both root causes strike simultaneously, the database experiences a feedback loop in which excessive CPU spin and context switching from latch contention coexist with, and intensify, host CPU saturation. Observable symptoms include: sustained 90-100 % CPU usage alongside a high fraction of CPU time spent in spin-wait; explosive run-queue growth paired with elevated buffer-busy, latch free, and scheduler wait events; steep, wide-ranging latency spikes where even simple statements stall behind both CPU scarcity and latch acquisition; and uneven throughput as hot pages intermittently freeze large parts of the workload while other sessions starve for CPU.

Causally, hot-page contention forces foreground processes to enter tight spin loops, burning CPU while waiting for latches; this self-generates the CPU Resource Anomaly. Conversely, a pre-existing CPU bottleneck lengthens critical sections inside the buffer manager because latch holders are scheduled less frequently, inflating the hold times seen by other sessions and deepening buffer contention. The two anomalies therefore reinforce each other: latch spin escalates CPU pressure, while CPU starvation magnifies latch hold durations, propagating stalls across the workload and driving the database into a mutually amplifying spiral of compute exhaustion and buffer-cache serialization.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds to wait for more data from a source/replica connection before aborting the read.
entry.trigger_condition: A replica waits longer than replica_net_timeout for more data from the source connection.
entry.workload_impact: The replication network read is aborted and the replica considers the connection interrupted.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL replication system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
